summary: A fast, tactical duel where each hero's unique deck of movement/attack/defense cards creates a distinct combat rhythm, with Robin Hood's crew sniping from range and stealing cards while Bigfoot smashes in for big hits before vanishing into the woods. Games are quick (20 minutes), decided by careful positioning, bluffing which card you'll play, and timing your special abilities against the opponent's hand.
praised: Deep asymmetry between heroes despite simple core rules
Fast setup and playtime, easy to teach
High production value (sculpted miniatures, dual-sided board)
No-luck combat resolution rewards skill and card-reading over dice
Great entry point into the wider Unmatched line, good for two players
criticised: Small card pool per hero means matches can become solved/repetitive with experience
Fixed 2-player set has less replay variety than 4-player Unmatched boxes
Bigfoot vs Robin Hood specifically seen as a slightly weaker/less iconic pairing than other sets
Line-of-sight/ranged rules can slow down play with board measuring disputes

interaction.kind: direct card-based combat and positional blocking

scoring.why: The match ends the instant one hero's life total is reduced to zero, so the whole game is about managing your own health and closing out attacks.

similar: Unmatched: Battle of Legends Volume One
